races.title: State House, District 91
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kyle Hall
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 91 since November 2015, when Gov. Pat McCrory appointed him. Before that he was communications director for U.S. Rep. Mark Walker. He is a licensed real estate broker and Realtor, and a UNC-Chapel Hill graduate (2012).

endorsements.text: His campaign website lists endorsements from U.S. Rep. Tim Moore (NC-14), N.C. House Speaker Destin Hall, Stokes County Sheriff Joey Lemons, Forsyth County Commissioner Gloria Whisenhunt and Walnut Cove Mayor Nellie Brown.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements by Kyle Hall on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, police pay, or campaign-money pledges. His only issue statements in the pages we had come from his 2016 campaign website, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no recorded actions (sponsored bills or official filings) tied to the issues voters care about. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026, so the endorsements above come only from his own site. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born September 5, 1990 and raised in Stokes County, and his campaign site says he was born and raised in the 91st House District.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since November 2015 (about 10 years), including chairing the Appropriations Committee. Earlier he was communications director for U.S. Rep. Mark Walker. He is a licensed real estate broker.
qual.why: A decade of legislative service plus congressional staff work puts him in the high band. The committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: A decade of legislative service plus congressional staff work puts him in the high band. The committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said "The most fundamental right is life. We must protect life and advocate for the unborn."

second-amendment.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said "Our right to keep and bear arms must be protected."

workers-first.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said "Illegal immigration must be stopped in North Carolina."

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His 2016 campaign website said teaching is a valuable profession and, while NC Republicans had raised teacher pay, "more must be done."

cands.name: Lucille Puckett
cands.bio: Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 91 in 2026. Nonprofit founder (Take Back Our H.O.O.D.S.), former NAACP Mecklenburg County vice chair, and former director of Project Pacts Today. She has not held elected office. She previously ran unsuccessfully for Charlotte mayor and for the state House and Senate.

endorsements.text: Listed as recommended in the 2026 voter guide 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Puckett was raised or when she moved to North Carolina. No record shows her taking a position on a ban or moratorium on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing pay, or abortion. Her website says she supports the Second Amendment while addressing gun violence, but it gives no specific policy. She has never held elected office, so there are no official actions to report. Sources do not specify her work history or dates for the nonprofit roles or the Charlotte Housing Authority board seat.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Founder of a nonprofit for families affected by violence, with an MBA and a social work degree. Director of Project Pacts Today, community advocate with the National Action Network and ACORN, and former NAACP Mecklenburg vice chair. No elected office held.
qual.why: She has real nonprofit and advocacy work and an MBA, but no legislative, policy-staff or budget career and no elected office. A housing authority board seat and civic roles add nothing under the rubric, so the score is low.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says growth should not overwhelm communities, and that residents deserve a voice on developments such as data centers that could affect land, water and roads. She promises transparency, protection of natural resources and community input, while still supporting responsible economic development.
